<noinclude><pagequality level="4" user="Yann" />{{rh|170|AITAREYÂ-ARA''N''YAKA.|}}{{rule}}</noinclude><section begin="aranyaka1 adhyaya2" />then, after having driven away evil, he becomes learned, long-lived, and full of austerities.

9. He recites the hymn {{lang|sa-Latl|kayâ ''s''ubhâ savayasa''h'' sanîlâ''h''}} (Rv. I, 165, 1).

10. In the verse {{lang|sa-Latl|â ''s''âsate prati haryanty ukthâ}} (Rv. I, 165, 4) the word {{lang|sa-Latl|ukthâ}} occurs. Verily, that day (the mahâvrata) is {{lang|sa-Latl|uktha}} (hymn). Endowed with the word {{lang|sa-Latl|uktha}}, the form of this day becomes perfect.

11. That hymn is called Kayâ''s''ubhîya<ref>Cf. Ait. Brâhm. V, 16.</ref>. Verily, that hymn, which is called Kayâ''s''ubhîya, is mutual understanding and it is lasting. By means of it Indra, Agastya, and the Maruts came to a mutual understanding. Therefore, if he recites the Kayâ''s''ubhîya hymn, it serves for mutual understanding.

12. The same hymn is also long life. Therefore, if the sacrificer is dear to the Hot''ri'', let him recite the Kayâ''s''ubhîya hymn for him.

13. He recites the hymn {{lang|sa-Latl|marutvâ''n'' indra v''ri''shabo ra''n''âya}} (Rv. Ill, 47, 1).

14. In it the words {{lang|sa-Latl|indra v''ri''shabha}} (powerful) occur. Verily, powerful is a form of Indra<ref>Cf. Ait. Âr. II, 2, 1, 8.</ref>, this day belongs to Indra, and this is the perfect form of that day.

15. That hymn is composed by Vi''s''vâmitra. Verily, Vi''s''vâmitra was the friend ({{lang|sa-Latl|mitra}}) of all ({{lang|sa-Latl|vi''s''va}}).

16. Everybody is the friend of him who knows this, and for whom a Hot''ri'' priest who knows this, recites this hymn.

17. The next hymn, {{lang|sa-Latl|''g''anish''th''â ugra''h'' sahase turâya}} (Rv. I, 73, 1), forms a Nividdhâna<ref>The hymn consists of eleven verses. In the middle, after the sixth verse, nivids or invocations, such as {{lang|sa-Latl|indro marutvân}}, are inserted, and therefore itis called a nividdhâna hymn.</ref>, and,<section end="aranyaka1 adhyaya2" /><noinclude>{{rule}}{{smallrefs}}</noinclude>
